## What
Modified `short_display_path` to preserve the root path `"/"` instead of collapsing it to an empty string.

## Why
When displaying the root directory as a path, the function previously returned an empty string, which is confusing in UI displays and logs.

## How
Added a check: if the trimmed path is empty, return `"/"` instead.
items.title: fix: preserve root path '/' in short_display_path

items.body:
## What
Added `skip_flag_values` logic to `parse_find_query_and_path` so flags and their values are skipped when extracting the path argument.

## Why
Commands like `find -type f .` were incorrectly parsing `.` as a query instead of the path, because the parser didn't account for flags consuming the next token.

## How
Introduced a `skip_flag_values` helper that skips common find flags (`-type`, `-name`, `-exec`, etc.) and their values, then finds the first non-flag, non-operator argument as the path.
items.title: fix: resolve path in 'find' when flags precede the path argument

items.body:
## What
Added logic to parse the `--search-path` flag in fd commands and use its value as the displayed path.

## Why
fd's `--search-path` flag specifies the directory to search, but the parser didn't recognize it, leaving the path field empty or incorrect.

## How
Extended the fd parsing logic to check for `--search-path` and extract its value into the `search_paths` vector, which is then used as the path if no positional path is found.
items.title: fix: extract path from fd --search-path flag

items.body:
## What
Extended update hints to detect and suggest the correct package manager (npm, pnpm, yarn, bun) based on lockfiles in the project.

## Why
Users who installed Codex via pnpm or yarn were shown npm-specific update commands, causing confusion.

## How
- Added lockfile detection (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lockb`, `package-lock.json`)
- Updated hint messages to show the appropriate package manager command
- Retained npm as fallback when no lockfile is detected
items.title: fix: add pnpm and yarn support to update hints and package manager detection

items.body:
## What
Modified `parse_find_query_and_path` to default the path to `"."` when no path is explicitly provided.

## Why
Commands like `find -name '*.rs'` have an implicit current directory search path, but the parser left the path as `None`, making the display incomplete.

## How
Added a check: if no path is found after parsing, set `path = Some(".")`.
items.title: fix: default find path to '.' when no path argument is given

items.body:
## What
Added support for `--regexp=` and `-e` (no space) forms in grep command parsing.

## Why
grep accepts both `--regexp=PATTERN` and `-ePATTERN` forms, but the parser only handled the space-separated versions.

## How
Extended `parse_grep_like` to detect:
- `--regexp=PATTERN` using `strip_prefix`
- `-ePATTERN` (no space) using `strip_prefix` when the remainder is non-empty

Added tests for both forms.
items.title: fix: parse --regexp=PATTERN and -ePATTERN (no space) in grep

## What
The Zero Data Retention troubleshooting section in `README.md` only listed `npm i -g @openai/codex@latest` as the upgrade command.

## Why
Users who installed Codex via pnpm, yarn, or bun would see an npm-specific command that does not apply to their setup, causing confusion.

Replaced the single npm command with a bullet list covering all four supported package managers:
- `npm i -g @openai/codex@latest`
- `pnpm add -g @openai/codex@latest`
- `yarn global add @openai/codex@latest`
- `bun install -g @openai/codex@latest`
items.title: fix: list all package managers in ZDR upgrade hint in README

## What
Added support for `--file=` and `-f` (no space) flag forms in grep command parsing.

## Why
grep accepts both `--file=patterns.txt` and `-fpatterns.txt` forms, but the parser only handled the space-separated versions `--file patterns.txt` and `-f patterns.txt`.

## How
Extended `parse_grep_like` to detect:
- `--file=PATTERN` using `strip_prefix`
- `-fPATTERN` (no space) using `strip_prefix` when the remainder is non-empty

Added tests for both forms.
items.title: fix: parse --file=PATTERN and -fPATTERN (no space) in grep

items.body:
## What
Added support for all ripgrep pattern/file flag forms: `-e`, `--regexp=`, `-f`, and `--file=` with both space-separated and no-space variants.

## Why
ripgrep accepts multiple forms for specifying patterns and pattern files, but the parser only handled positional patterns. This caused commands like `rg -efoo src` or `rg --regexp=foo src` to incorrectly parse the pattern.

## How
- Added pattern extraction logic that checks for `-e`, `--regexp`, `-f`, and `--file` flags
- Handles both space-separated (`-e foo`) and no-space (`-efoo`, `--regexp=foo`) forms
- Stores extracted pattern in `pattern_override` and uses it instead of the first positional arg
- Added `skip_flag_values` entries for these flags so they don't get treated as paths
- Added comprehensive tests for all forms
items.title: fix: parse -ePATTERN, --regexp=PATTERN, -fPATTERN, --file=PATTERN in rg

## Why

PR #12584 became difficult to review as a single feature diff. This PR isolates the `shell-escalation` prep work so later `exec-server` and `core` changes can be reviewed against a stable API.

The main goal is to make `shell-escalation` reusable from multiple callers without hard-coding a dependency on `codex-core` internals.

## What Changed

- Introduce a reusable executor interface in `shell-escalation` (`ShellCommandExecutor`) and thread it through `unix::escalate_server::run_escalate_server`.
- Move sandbox execution inputs needed by `shell-escalation` into a crate-local `SandboxState` type.
- Open up the `unix` module API surface needed by downstream callers (`pub mod unix`, public `ShellEscalationPolicy`).
- Tighten socket handling in `unix/socket.rs` (explicit `try_io` error handling and `Socket::pair_raw` for Unix socketpairs).
- Add a temporary compatibility shim in `shell-escalation/src/lib.rs` so existing callers continue to build while the stacked follow-up PRs land.

## Verification

- No standalone verification run after splitting this prep refactor out of the larger zsh-fork change.
- The follow-up stacked PRs adopt this API (`#12615` and the remaining `core`/test changes), which exercises the integration path.

This is the `exec-server` follow-up to the `shell-escalation` API prep in #12614, split out of PR #12584 to keep review scope smaller.

Separating the `exec-server` adoption from the `core` zsh-fork migration makes it easier to review the adapter wiring and confirm this remains behavior-preserving.

### What
Fix `/review` so it uses the active runtime turn context when selecting model config, especially reasoning effort, instead of relying on potentially stale startup config.

### Why
Fixes #12495. After switching model/effort in-session (for example to `gpt-5.1-codex-mini` + `high`), `/review` could still use startup effort (for example `xhigh`) and fail with unsupported-effort errors.

### How
Updated review flow in `core/src/codex.rs`:
* Review now derives config from `parent_turn_context.config` instead of startup config.
* Added a shared helper, `select_reasoning_effort_for_model(...)`, and reused it in both model switching and review.
* Review now sets `per_turn_config.model_reasoning_effort` from that helper, preserving current runtime effort when supported and falling back when not.

### Testing
Added/updated coverage in `core/tests/suite/review.rs`:
* `review_uses_current_reasoning_effort_after_model_switch`
* `review_falls_back_reasoning_effort_when_current_effort_is_unsupported`

Validation run:
* `cargo clippy -p codex-core --tests`
* `cargo test -p codex-core`

## Summary

`codex exec` prints the agent's response twice in interactive use — once to stderr during streaming and again to stdout in `print_final_output()`. This PR skips the stdout copy when stdout is a TTY so interactive users see the message only once. Piped/redirected stdout (`codex exec "…" > out.txt`) is unaffected.

## Root cause

`EventProcessorWithHumanOutput` prints the agent message to stderr as events arrive (`AgentMessage` handler), then unconditionally reprints it to stdout after the turn completes. The existing code had a comment acknowledging the duplication but only attempted to mitigate it visually with a token-summary separator.

## Fix

Added a `std::io::stdout().is_terminal()` guard in `print_final_output()` so the stdout copy is only emitted when stdout is redirected to a file or pipe.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p codex-exec` — compiles clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p codex-exec` — no warnings
- [x] `cargo test -p codex-exec` — all 25 tests pass
- [ ] Manual: `codex exec "Print 5 cities"` — output appears once
- [ ] Manual: `codex exec "Print 5 cities" > out.txt` — file contains the response

Fixes https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/12566
items.title: fix(exec): suppress duplicate output when stdout is a terminal

items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds support for a project-local `mcp.json` file in the current working directory (`cwd/mcp.json`) so MCP server launchers can be configured per-repo/session without modifying global `~/.codex/config.toml`.

### Supported `mcp.json` shapes

- `{ "mcpServers": { ... } }`
- `{ ... }` (direct server map)

## Motivation

Enhancement request: support local MCP server configuration for the current directory.

This enables project-scoped MCP setup with lower friction and cleaner separation from global user config.

## What changed

1. Config loader now reads `cwd/mcp.json` (CWD only) and maps it into `mcp_servers`.
2. Local `mcp.json` entries are merged into the CWD project layer and override same-name `mcp_servers` entries from other layers for the active session.
3. Loading is trust-gated using existing project trust logic:
   - trusted project: local config is active
   - untrusted/unknown project: layer is disabled, local MCP config not applied
4. Error handling follows trust model:
   - trusted + invalid `mcp.json`: fail config load with file-specific parse error
   - untrusted/unknown + invalid `mcp.json`: ignored with disabled layer behavior
5. Docs updated to describe local `mcp.json`, supported shapes, precedence, and trust gating.

## Tests

Added loader tests covering:

- local override precedence over user/project `mcp_servers`
- direct-map JSON shape support
- use without `.codex/config.toml` in CWD
- untrusted project disable behavior
- invalid trusted `mcp.json` failure
- invalid untrusted `mcp.json` ignored
- inline `bearer_token` rejection in local config

## Notes on local validation

- `just fmt` could not be run in this environment because `just` is not installed and network access is unavailable for installing it.
- touched Rust files were formatted with `rustfmt` directly.
- `cargo test -p codex-core` could not run because local Cargo is `1.83.0` and this workspace requires `edition2024` support from a newer toolchain.
items.title: Add support for local cwd mcp.json MCP server config
